limits: Zero records found meet the strict bar of being simultaneously new, human-species-confirmed, purified-enzyme and primary-value-inspected. Every ledger row is marked strict_new_biochemical_holdout_eligible = 'no'.

The MRK-952 dossier does not state the assay species or protein construct, so those records cannot enter a species-confirmed holdout until confirmed from a primary source. This is an explicit blocking condition in the evaluation design.
The SGC dossier is direct producer evidence, not a peer-reviewed dedicated MRK-952 assay publication; the 2026 degrader paper describes that work as forthcoming.
The SGC page's prose 'IC50' and its figure's 'EC50' labels disagree; both are recorded separately and must not be treated as two independent observations.
MRK-952-NC must not be used as an inactive decoy: it is a weak inhibitor, and its stereochemistry is explicitly 'assumed' by the source.

Publisher paywalls blocked full text and supporting information for 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6b01786 and 10.1002/cmdc.201800398, including the latter's Table_1.xlsx / Table_2.xlsx proteomics tables that would resolve the Kinobead measurements. These are access limits, not evidence of absence; those rows remain database-supported and primary-value-not-inspected.
Two Europe PMC full-text fetches returned HTTP 500 and one ACS supplement returned an HTTP 202 reCAPTCHA interstitial; these were worked around via Europe PMC XML or publisher pages where possible.

Not searched at all: patents, PubChem BioAssay deposits, thesis repositories, non-English literature, vendor screening-library data, and 533 of the 633 broad Europe PMC hits. Any may contain further records.
The targeted Europe PMC query (58 hits, all 58 retrieved) is bounded, not an exhaustive census of public NUDT5 literature.

Novelty/overlap was computed only against the 14 unique Balikci ChEMBL graphs retrieved here. It was NOT computed against the repository's 45 structures or the original 23-compound source CSV, because no repository file was inspected; repository_overlap is recorded as 'not assessed' and must be recomputed before any external-test claim.

The primary proposed test is a single disjoint pair, so it can falsify a potency-discrimination claim but cannot confirm one (coin-flip probability 0.5). The design cannot estimate AUC, enrichment, precision, calibration or generalization.

Source independence is not the same as scaffold independence or never-before-inspected data; TH5427 and the EUbOPEN row are explicitly flagged as pre-inspected reference context rather than new evidence.
Cell-viability IC50 values from the docking/MD literature (2020, 2022, 2025 papers) are deliberately excluded; importing them as biochemical labels would inflate apparent external validation.

No repository was read or edited, no commit/PR/session/deposit/outreach occurred, no model was trained, and no data selection was optimized. Nothing here supports any claim about acceptance, publication, or prospective success.
evidence.summary: Bounded read-only primary-source investigation of public NUDT5 biochemical evidence beyond Balikci 2024 is complete. The actionable new angle is not a new dataset but a structurally disjoint, externally produced probe pair (SGC/MSD MRK-952 and its matched weak control MRK-952-NC) with machine-readable, independently re-verified structures and a ~100-fold measured potency separation; it supports a falsification test, not a benchmark. Complete uncapped target queries show the wider public record is far smaller than row counts suggest: 50 raw database rows reduce to a handful of non-Balikci measurements, zero Ki records, and zero records that are simultaneously new, human-species-confirmed, purified-enzyme and primary-value-inspected. Seven data/report artifacts plus a full request manifest and 29 MB raw-snapshot archive were uploaded. No repository file was read or edited, no model trained, no data selection optimized.
verified_findings: Target identity resolved unambiguously: human NUDT5 = UniProt Q9UKK9 = ChEMBL CHEMBL4105713 ('ADP-sugar pyrophosphatase', tax 9606); the ChEMBL free-text target search returns exactly one target, so there is no sibling-target ambiguity.

Complete uncapped target queries returned 29 ChEMBL activity rows and 21 BindingDB affinity rows (50 raw rows) against ChEMBL_37 (released 2026-05-01). Endpoint breakdown ChEMBL/BindingDB: IC50 13/10, EC50 7/7, Kd 4/4, ED50 2/0, qualitative 'Activity' 3/0, and Ki 0/0.

After publication-level deduplication, 22 of 29 ChEMBL rows and 17 of 21 BindingDB rows are Balikci 2024 (10.1021/acs.jmedchem.4c00072), which was treated as already-curated and excluded from new-data counts per instruction.

ChEMBL and BindingDB are mirrors here, not corroborating sources: the BindingDB NUDT5 ligand page states its record was 'Curated by ChEMBL'. Deduplication was therefore done on recomputed canonical isomeric SMILES/InChIKey plus publication DOI, not on row counts.

Provenance trap found and documented: the BindingDB REST response preserves the '>' relation on the 2017 counter-screen, while the BindingDB ligand web page renders it as 'IC50: 1.00E+5nM' with no relation. Reading the page instead of the API would silently convert a censored inactive into an exact value.

SGC/MSD MRK-952 is the one actionable new angle: the producer dossier reports NUDT5 IC50 85 nM (AMP-Glo, ADP-ribose substrate) versus MRK-952-NC IC50 10 micromolar, plus orthogonal SPR KD 0.031 +/- 0.018 micromolar versus 1.380 +/- 0.380 micromolar (n=2).

MRK-952 structures were independently re-verified rather than trusted: RDKit recomputation from the SGC CSV isomeric SMILES reproduced the published InChIKey and molecular formula exactly for both probe and control (CAPZLSKZPWSIKV-LJQANCHMSA-N and HSIKTHHVIIENBG-SFHVURJKSA-N).

The probe pair is chemically disjoint from existing chemistry: max Morgan(r=2, 2048-bit, chirality-aware) Tanimoto to any retrieved Balikci ChEMBL graph is 0.187 (MRK-952) and 0.157 (MRK-952-NC), and neither exact graph appears in any retrieved ChEMBL or BindingDB target row.

Endpoint-labelling discrepancy captured: the SGC page prose says 'IC50', but its own biochemical figure labels the fits EC50 (MRK-952 0.0849 micromolar, 95% CI 0.0815-0.0883; NC 10.6 micromolar, 9.62-11.8). Both are recorded separately and never counted as two observations.
MRK-952-NC is a weak inhibitor, not an inactive, and the SGC figure states 'single isomer, stereochemistry assumed'. Scoring it as a decoy would be incorrect.

The 2026 Nature Communications NUDT5 degrader paper (PMC13462928) cites MRK-952 by the exact SGC URL and states the probe work is 'to be published', corroborating the probe's existence and use while confirming no dedicated peer-reviewed assay paper was accessible.

Non-Balikci measured records are limited to: one censored NUDT5 IC50 > 100000 nM counter-screen (10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6b01786) and two Kinobead competitive pull-down apparent Kd values of 3616.841 and 7684.474 nM (10.1002/cmdc.201800398), which are lysate-competition binding numbers rather than purified-enzyme inhibition.
Double-counting hazard identified: ChEMBL re-expresses the same 2018 NVP-BHG712 Kinobead measurements as both Kd(app) and ED50 rows, so stacking both endpoints would duplicate two experiments.

Two apparently-extra sources collapse on inspection: 10.1016/j.ejmech.2024.116540 is a 2024 review whose NUDT5 row restates Balikci, and EUbOPEN dataset CHEMBL5723035 (TH5427 IC50 29 nM) carries a provenance field pointing back to Page 2018. Neither is an independent study.

Known-reference check confirmed from two independent primary sources: PDB 5NWH ligand 9CH (InChIKey QXCXMVYVUHVFLP-UHFFFAOYSA-N) matches the ChEMBL TH5427 graph exactly with an unsubstituted distal piperazine nitrogen, and the Page 2018 supplement names compound 28 (TH5427) as the 8-(piperazin-1-yl) purinedione while the adjacent compound 26 (TH5424) is the 4-ethylpiperazine. Reported as confirmation of the already-identified N-methyl discrepancy, not as a discovery.

Page 2018 primary text verified the assay basis for the reference value: enzyme-coupled malachite green (MG) assay, with the supplement giving 29.1 nM and the main text/EUbOPEN rounding to 29 nM, i.e. one observation, not two.

Category error averted in the computational literature: the inspected 2020 approved-drug repurposing, 2022 coumarin (55.57 +/- 0.7 ug/mL) and 2025 fluvoxamine (53.86 +/- 0.05 micromolar) papers measure MCF-7 cell viability by MTT, not NUDT5 turnover. The fluvoxamine abstract was read directly and reports a docking score of -8.514 kcal/mol plus an MTT IC50; all were excluded from the biochemical ledger.

Honest final tally recorded in the artifacts: 8 ledger measurement rows across 6 unique graphs, 0 Ki records, and 0 rows meeting the strict new/human-confirmed/purified-enzyme/primary-inspected bar (strict_new_biochemical_holdout_eligible = 'no' for every row).

Reproducibility verified rather than asserted: all 41 HTTP requests are logged with URL, UTC timestamp, status, content type, byte count and SHA-256 (32x200, 6x403, 2x500, 1x202 reCAPTCHA interstitial); all 41 stored response bodies were re-hashed at ledger build time and matched, and the build script regenerates every artifact offline while asserting the structural identity checks.

limits: No repositories were inspected or modified; no commits, pushes, PRs, sessions, contacts or deposit changes were made. Dataset counts and project mappings NC5-02=ACT-19=compound 11 and ACT-20=compound 10 were accepted from the brief, not independently re-audited.

Investigation was limited to two targeted literature searches, Page/Balikci primary articles and selected supplements, five structural deposits, six assemblies and four CCD identities. Exhaustive later literature, patents, all PDB entries and compound availability were not searched. Wright's earlier nuclear-ATP paper was not independently read.

Balikci source data were used only as existing evidence for experimental design, not presented as newly discovered external data. Reported cross-target IC50 ratios are provisional: the original enzyme reactions used different incubation times, and ratios are not KD/Ki or statistical confidence bounds.

No docking, MD, new contact-distance calculation, structure-factor analysis, electron-density re-refinement or experimental testing was performed. Proposed mutants and catalytic-dead rescue constructs require independent validation.

Missing modeled metal does not establish metal-independent catalysis; deposited assemblies do not alone prove solution oligomer equilibria; missing residues, occupancy issues and construct discrepancies limit atom-level interpretation.

Structure analysis alone cannot establish cellular selectivity, dose-dependent occupancy, protein degradation, noncatalytic protein functions, permeability, efficacy or clinical relevance. Neither compound 9 nor compound 13 should be treated as an unqualified target-specific cellular control.
The experimental plan is falsifiable but untested. No manufactured biological results, efficacy claims, novelty guarantees or acceptance guarantees are provided.
evidence.summary: Completed a bounded, read-only primary-source investigation and uploaded six artifacts. Recommended project direction: use the same compound-9 ligand in NUDT5/8RIY and NUDT14/8OTV to test differential recognition, then combine orthogonal inhibitors, target-engagement measurements and genetic rescue to distinguish NUDT5 catalytic inhibition, NUDT14 contribution and protein-loss effects. This is a proposed project direction, not a literature-novelty claim or newly discovered training data.
verified_findings: 5NWH is human NUDT5–TH5427, CCD 9CH, at 2.60 Å. 5NQR is human NUDT5–TH1713, CCD 958, at 2.20 Å. CCD 9CH specifies C20H20Cl2N8O3, InChIKey QXCXMVYVUHVFLP-UHFFFAOYSA-N, and a 1,3-dimethyl xanthine core.
Relevant Balikci deposits are 8RDZ, NUDT5–ibrutinib/A1H14 at 2.02 Å; 8RIY, NUDT5–compound 9/W0O at 2.288 Å; and 8OTV, NUDT14–compound 9/W0O at 1.82 Å.

All five deposits describe human proteins expressed in E. coli, without deposited sequence mutations. All deposited biological assemblies are dimers; 8RDZ has four protein chains in the asymmetric unit but two separate dimers, A/C and B/D.

Modeled Mg counts per asymmetric unit for 5NWH, 5NQR, 8RDZ, 8RIY and 8OTV are respectively 0, 0, 8, 0 and 1. Corresponding unmodeled-residue counts are 50, 48, 115, 31 and 23. Extracted mmCIF counts agree with RCSB entry API totals.

Paper-versus-deposit construct discrepancies remain explicit: Page describes NUDT5 residues 1–210 but 5NWH/5NQR deposit 1–219 sequences; Balikci describes 1–208 but 8RDZ deposits 1–219. 8RIY contains NUDT5 1–208 plus Ser0, and 8OTV contains NUDT14 1–222 plus Ser0.

5NQR has three ligand records at occupancies 0.5, 0.5 and 1.0, not three full-occupancy binding sites. 8RIY author chains AAA/BBB map to label chains A/B; AAA Arg51 CZ has zero occupancy. Exact missing ranges and flagged atoms are retained in the artifacts.

Page and Balikci describe different recognition environments involving NUDT5 Arg51 versus the NUDT14 pocket. Testing differential Arg51 dependence is a hypothesis grounded in published assignments; no new contacts or binding energies were calculated.

The already-curated Balikci Table 1 and CSV report NUDT5/NUDT14 IC50 values of 0.270/0.162 µM for compound 9, 0.487/0.263 µM for compound 10, and 2.04/0.519 µM for compound 11. Compound 13 is >50/3.72 µM, making it a provisional NUDT14-biased biochemical comparator, not a validated selective cellular probe. Compounds 12 and 15 are assayed inactive against both at the reported >50 µM threshold.
Balikci compound 9 retains BTK cellular engagement: EC50 0.377 µM versus NUDT5 NanoBRET EC50 1.08 µM. Its NUDT14 HiBiT-CETSA stabilization was measured at 30 µM, not as a cellular potency curve.

Page reports TH5427 NUDT5 IC50 29 nM and NUDT14 inhibition of 38% at 100 µM, not a verified NUDT14 dose-response IC50. Its biological results concern hormone-stimulated T47D cells, not generic breast-cancer killing. DARTS measures protease protection after lysis, not drug-induced protein loss.

Delivered a report, five-row structural metadata CSV, nine-row compound/control panel, eight-step falsifiable experimental plan, 16-claim evidence ledger, and reproducibility bundle. Artifact parsing and structural consistency checks passed; the source manifest records 29 successful primary-source downloads.

limits: No repository inspection, edits, commits, pushes, PRs, new sessions, outreach, deposit changes, model fitting/scoring, docking, simulations or experiments occurred.

The 45-structure counts, 19 positives/26 unassayed decoys, project identity mappings, known TH5427 graph error and supplied structural-file caveats were accepted as context, not independently re-audited.
Scientific expansion stopped after one citation hop from the 2026 degrader study to the 2025 Science study. This was not an exhaustive novelty or literature search.

Not searched or repeated: broad literature/database census, patents, PubChem BioAssay, vendors/availability/prices, all later citations, actual repository overlap, raw assay reanalysis, new PDB/contact or structure-factor analysis, supplementary-data re-audit, and the original nuclear-ATP study cited by Page.

The 2025 Europe PMC XML endpoint returned HTTP 500; its primary full text was successfully retrieved and inspected through PMC HTML. Downloading a complete article does not imply every figure, supplement or raw dataset was audited.
The 2025 and 2026 mechanistic papers share investigators and the degrader toolkit and are not wholly independent replications.

MRK-952 purified-assay species and construct remain unresolved. Human-cell use does not identify the purified-enzyme construct; a strict species-confirmed human biochemical holdout claim remains blocked.

The probe-pair outcomes are already exposed. A correct single ordering is only one concordant pair; under a symmetric random-order null its probability is one half. A reverse order contradicts that pair-specific prediction, not every possible use of the model.

Y74E catalytic competence in the published ADP-ribose assay does not establish its ATP-producing activity, PPAT binding, expression or localization in T47D. Those properties, same-line context competence and cellular engagement/selectivity windows are prerequisites, not demonstrated outcomes here.

The proposed prospective validation has not been executed or operationally locked. Sample sizes, meaningful-effect/equivalence margins and exposure windows must be justified from independent qualification/pilot work before confirmatory measurements; none were fabricated.
Feasibility rankings are conditional on laboratory platforms and reagent access that were not checked. The three extensions remain hypotheses, not measured discoveries.

Venue assessments reflect inspected official scopes and scientific judgment, not acceptance probabilities. No new biological data, clinical efficacy, exhaustive novelty, or publication acceptance guarantee is provided.
study.summary: Completed a bounded, read-only research-extension investigation and uploaded seven deliverables. Ranked hypotheses: (1) context-specific separation of NUDT5 catalysis from PPAT-binding function using qualified E112Q/Y74E rescue experiments; (2) differential Arg51-dependent ligand recognition and prospective NUDT5/NUDT14 selectivity; (3) a frozen, no-tuning MRK-952/NC retrospective diagnostic. The pivotal novelty constraint is that general NUDT5–PPAT scaffolding and catalytic-inhibitor/protein-loss discordance are already published. Delivered a concise report, falsification matrix, all six evidence categories, separate retrospective/prospective validation designs, empirical experimental gates, realistic venue-fit/rejection arguments, and a reproducible evidence bundle. No repositories were inspected or modified, and no model scores or experimental results were generated.
verified_findings: Downloaded and read both supplied research reports; their broad database and structural audits were not repeated. The supplied Balikci structures were treated as already-curated evidence, not newly discovered external data.

Directly inspected the SGC/MSD MRK-952 dossier and two figures. Prose reports biochemical IC50 values of 85 nM for MRK-952 and 10 micromolar for MRK-952-NC; the curve figure labels its fits EC50, 0.0849 and 10.6 micromolar. These are not independent observations. NC stereochemistry is explicitly assumed, and NC is a weak inhibitor rather than an inactive compound.

The inspected SGC SPR figure reports NUDT5 KD values of 0.031 ± 0.018 and 1.380 ± 0.380 micromolar, n=2, for MRK-952 and NC. It marks NUDT14 as nonbinding and annotates catalytic inactivity, but does not specify the quantitative inactivity cutoff.

Directly inspected Balikci 2024 Results/Figs. 3–5 and Methods. Compound 9 binds NUDT5 and NUDT14 and retains BTK cellular engagement. NUDT5 NanoBRET EC50 is 1.08 micromolar versus BTK EC50 0.377 micromolar; NUDT14 CETSA was measured at 30 micromolar, not as a calibrated occupancy curve. NUDT5 and NUDT14 catalytic assays used different incubation times.

Directly inspected Page 2018 Fig. 4 and associated Results. Its TH5427 findings concern hormone-stimulated nuclear ATP readout, gene regulation and proliferation in T47D models, not generic breast-cancer-cell killing.

Directly inspected Marques 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-74489-9. TH5427 and MRK-952 did not phenocopy NUDT5 knockout in the tested 6-thioguanine setting; degradation and E112Q reconstitution support a protein-dependent contribution.

Followed one pivotal citation to Nguyen 2025, DOI 10.1126/science.adv4257, and inspected its primary full text. NUDT5–PPAT interaction and nonenzymatic repression of purine synthesis are already reported. Y74E disrupts PPAT binding with retained catalytic activity in the reported ADP-ribose assay; E112Q provides the complementary catalytic-deficient comparison. These alleles require requalification for the proposed hormone-response experiment.

The strongest proposed extension uses the published separation-of-function tools in a qualified, same-cell-model context comparison. Using different cell lines for the hormone and purine arms would confound context with cell identity; the report explicitly limits such an inference.

The retrospective plan freezes structures, model/configuration, score interpretation, processing and baselines before scoring, with no tuning. One exposed probe pair cannot establish generalization, calibration, AUC, enrichment or superiority. Prospective validation instead requires independently qualified assays, a timestamped analysis lock, blinded samples and genuinely uninspected outcomes; known-compound remeasurement remains control or replication evidence.

The report provides six falsification rows and six experimental gates. Gates depend on identity, assay qualification, mutant integrity, measured cellular engagement, independently justified precision and prespecified contrasts—not invented potency, viability or fold-change success thresholds.

Official ACS Chemical Biology, ACS Medicinal Chemistry Letters and JCIM author guidelines were inspected. Conditional venue fit and specific rejection arguments are supplied; none of the current planning artifacts is presented as a publication-ready original experimental result.

Uploaded a 2,308-word report, a six-row falsification CSV, a 21-claim evidence ledger spanning Demonstrated, Strongly supported, Suggestive, Hypothesized, Unknown and Refuted, a validation/gates JSON, a source register, an artifact-validation record and an evidence bundle.

Verification passed: JSON/CSV parsing, category completeness, source-reference checks, four exact quotations checked against raw primary XML/HTML, 12 downloaded-response SHA-256 checks, deterministic regeneration, Python compilation, ZIP integrity and portable offline regeneration with identical artifact bytes. Direct retrievals comprised 11 HTTP 200 responses and one HTTP 500 response.
